column1: # Rust vs on-demand: worker memory decision trail
# task: reduce siela podman stack RAM
# host: root@192.168.1.3, 15,406 MB RAM, 8 cores, kernel pressure avg10 0.00

column2: what
column3: why
column4: evidence
column5: result

column2: Measure the live stack before designing a rewrite.
column3: A RAM change needs a baseline or the "before" is a guess.
column4: podman cgroup memory.stat per service on 192.168.1.3.
column5: 468 MB private memory across the whole siela stack.

column2: Test the premise that RAM is under pressure.
column3: The user described active RAM obsession, so first check whether the host is actually constrained.
column4: free -m, /proc/pressure/memory, journalctl OOM grep, swap use.
column5: VERIFIED no pressure. 13,699 MB available, 8 KB swap used, zero OOM kills in 14 days, pressure avg10/60/300 all 0.00.

column2: Locate the real memory history.
column3: Recent commits #45 and #46 both target llama.cpp memory, which suggests the past fire was the LLM, not the workers.
column4: git log titles: "cap the host prompt cache that can grow to 8 GB", "use one server slot to trim host memory".
column5: INCONCLUSIVE for intent, consistent with the LLM having been the actual problem. Already fixed.

column2: Measure Bun worker floor, not just totals.
column3: To size a Rust saving you need to know what Bun itself costs.
column4: Bare Bun container 1 MB anon. Bun + discord.js + @discordjs/voice 27 MB. Full idle worker 52 MB.
column5: The app adds 25 MB over the libs; the libs add 26 MB over the runtime.

column2: Build a real Rust voice bot and measure it.
column3: A rust estimate from reading code is a guess.
column4: serenity 0.12 + songbird 0.4 built on host, cgroup anon and /proc RSS.
column5: VERIFIED 1.0 MB cgroup anon, 6.7 MB RSS, 10 threads, client constructed and songbird registered.

column2: Project the Rust saving for two workers.
column3: Convert the measurement into the decision number.
column4: First pass used an estimate of 20 MB connected, which turned out to be 10x too high for the bare bot.
column5: Superseded by D9.

column2: Measure both live on the same token and guild.
column3: The first comparison mixed a measured Bun number with an estimated Rust number.
column4: Stopped siela-voice-2, ran the Rust bot on its token, reached READY with guilds=1, measured cgroup memory, restored voice-2 to healthy and re-registered in the router.
column5: VERIFIED Bun 53 MB current vs Rust 2 MB current. Bare bot saves 51 MB. Complete worker projects to 8 to 20 MB, so 33 to 45 MB saved per worker.

column2: Restore production and clean up.
column3: Borrowing a token touched a live worker.
column4: podman healthcheck run siela-voice-2 exit 0, all three nodes present in GET /v1/music/nodes, 15 containers running, no test containers left.
column5: VERIFIED fleet restored.

column2: Test the 50-worker scaling argument.
column3: User's claim, and the 0.55% framing was anchored to 2 workers.
column4: Arithmetic at 50 always-on: 2,050 MB saved, 13% of host RAM.
column5: CONCEDED. The absolute figure is real; the earlier percentage was narrow.

column2: Measure the cost of one active stream.
column3: A fleet at scale is mostly active streams, not idle bots.
column4: cgroup anon 91 MB with yt-dlp, mpv, and ffmpeg live.
column5: Stream subprocesses cost 91 MB and are identical in Rust. At 50 concurrent that is 4,550 MB untouched by a rewrite.

column2: Measure CPU per stream.
column3: Guessed CPU would be the real wall at 50.
column4: 0.013 cores, verified by 2,812 KB of PCM consumed in 15s, matching 48k stereo s16.
column5: WRONG GUESS. 50 streams need 0.7 of 8 cores. CPU is not the limit.

column2: Measure on-demand cold start.
column3: On-demand is only viable if the delay is tolerable.
column4: voice-2 log timestamps, restart to gateway login.
column5: 2.3 seconds. Discord IDENTIFY dominates; Rust saves a few hundred ms.

column2: Compare options at 5 concurrent of 50 capacity.
column3: The fleet size may be capacity rather than concurrency.
column4: On-demand Bun 720 MB, always-on Rust 1,055 MB, on-demand Rust 515 MB.
column5: On-demand Bun beats always-on Rust by 335 MB. Break-even at about 11 concurrent streams.

column2: Shift recommendation to on-demand first.
column3: It is the larger multiplier at any fleet size and it measures real peak concurrency.
column4: D11 through D15.
column5: Recommendation issued. Rust is justified only if measured peak concurrency is near fleet size.

column2: Build the Rust worker anyway, on operator instruction.
column3: Operator chose to proceed with the rewrite and the queue.
column4: D16 noted the RAM case was weak; the decision was the operator's.
column5: Rust worker written, 11 modules, 8 tests, build green, zero warnings.

column2: Verify decode before designing around it.
column3: In-process decoding is the whole memory argument.
column4: Crate built, decoded a real AAC capture, 217 packets and 5.0 seconds.
column5: warning: songbird ships symphonia with default features off, so the crate must enable aac and isomp4.

column2: Live join attempt.
column3: Static reasoning cannot prove a voice connection works.
column4: Real gateway login with worker 2's token, then a join.
column5: FAILED twice. 4006 stale session, then 4017 "E2EE/DAVE protocol required".

column2: Find why the TypeScript worker joins but Rust does not.
column3: Same Discord, same guild, same channel.
column4: @discordjs/voice 0.19.2 ships davey. songbird 0.6.1 has DAVE via davey; 0.4 does not.
column5: songbird 0.6 fixes it with no source changes.

column2: Live playback after the upgrade.
column3: Prove audio actually plays, not just that it joins.
column4: Live radio stream and a normal track.
column5: VERIFIED. Live stream used ffmpeg 69 MB plus worker 12 MB. Normal track used 3 MB anon and 16 MB total, one process, no decoder.

column2: Check whether active playback costs change.
column3: If the dominant cost is subprocesses, a language rewrite cannot touch it.
column4: Temporary container, real yt-dlp resolve plus mpv playback.
column5: INCONCLUSIVE on steady state, but peak 88 MB and all of it in yt-dlp and mpv child processes.

column2: Recommend against Rust as a RAM fix.
column3: The measured saving does not address a constraint that exists.
column4: D2 plus D6.
column5: Recommendation issued. Rust remains defensible for non-RAM reasons.
